The ADR contradicts itself on command-id granularity. A per-target id is implied by: one DispatchRecordLatch per pass (l.1183; the latch exists for a loop that builds one command per target, server.cpp:13225-13230), 'each issuance makes one synchronous record_command_dispatch write' (the PERF-R2-2 throughput bound), and 'every issuance mints a fresh id'. But the CH-R2-1 forward sends one fresh command id per (cluster, action). Both cannot hold: per-target ids cannot ride one SendCommandRequest, and one id per forward makes the record and throughput model wrong for gateway agents. Separately, ADR-0074 D5 (adr-0074 l.96) binds every command signature to the agent id, and l.1228 says __resync__ takes no D5 exemption, so one signed CommandRequest cannot serve 2,000 agents once wave 2 lands. Today's forward_gateway_pending sends one agent per SendCommand (server.cpp:13902ff), so the multi-agent shape is new and has no precedent to inherit. Derived MEDIUM.
summary: A batched gateway forward carries one command id and one signature for up to 2,000 agents; that contradicts the ADR's per-target record and latch model and ADR-0074 D5's per-agent signature binding

trigger: Server stop() while the issuer is inside a slow steady-state Postgres call (a re-claim audit write before a pass, the kill-switch read, or the record insert)
classification_rationale: D8 l.1245-1250 says the in-flight call's statement is bounded by 'the drain's SET LOCAL statement_timeout of 1 s' and gives a worst case of 4+1+5+4+1 = 15 s. D6 l.839-843 applies that timeout only to stop-time drain writes. Steady-state calls run under the pool defaults: statement_timeout_ms = 30000 and lock_timeout_ms = 10000 (server/core/src/pg/pg_pool.hpp l.90/l.95). AuditStore::log is 'lease + log_in_txn + count_committed' on an autocommit lease (audit_store.hpp l.311-317; audit_store.cpp l.426-436), so a SET LOCAL has nothing to bind to inside it. The drain must open an explicit transaction and call log_in_txn. The true worst case is about 4+30+10 = 45 s. The server's systemd unit and compose files allow 210 s (deploy/systemd/yuzu-server.service TimeoutStopSec=210), so the impact is degraded only.
summary: The 15 s shutdown bound assumes the drain's 1 s statement_timeout also bounds an in-flight steady-state call, which runs under the pool's 30 s default; and SET LOCAL cannot apply inside AuditStore::log's autocommit lease

The backlog alert's closed cause list (l.1529-1533) and the diagnosis row (l.1567) were written earlier by SRE3-R3-1 (545531c43). They name 'a kill switch on __resync__' / 'the __resync__ kill switch', and D8 uses that phrase for the whole-action switch as distinct from the per-OS one. l.1532 also says 'the runbook separates the causes by the issuer's WARN log', but send_to's per-OS refusal (agent_registry.cpp l.752) and a dead stream return a bare false with no log; only gateway_capability_missing logs WARN today. Separating the causes needs the extracted check function to return a reason, which the ADR does not state.
summary: The send_failed cause lists in the backlog alert and diagnosis table omit the per-OS withhold added by ARCH-R3-1, and the WARN-log separation of causes depends on a reason return the shared check does not have

trigger: A multi-agent gateway resync forward (one SendCommand, up to 2,000 agent_ids) in which any one target does not send a terminal reply before the server's 10 s deadline (an agent busy or wedged, or one whose reply is delayed). Also true of every multi-agent forward: the response stream carries up to 2,000 per-agent SendCommandResponse frames.
classification_rationale: ARCH-R3-2 (89126f315) and CH-R2-3 (57ffaa71c) introduced the multi-agent forward, and CH-R2-2 (26d44b39c) set timeout_seconds equal to the client deadline. The ADR never says what the issuer's forwarder does with the response stream or how a forward's outcome is split across its agents. (1) The only classifier today, classify_gateway_forward_response (server/core/src/gateway_mgmt_stub_pool.hpp:307), compares each frame with ONE expected_agent_id. Reused as is, it flags 1,999 of 2,000 frames as kAgentMismatch, logging 'possible cross-cluster response forgery' at ERROR for each and moving yuzu_server_gateway_forward_total{status=agent_mismatch}. Skipping it loses the HA WS-4 4.3 forgery and not_connected checks on this path. The forwarder needs a membership-set check, and must say whether frames go to process_gateway_response. (2) The client deadline (now+10 s, set before the call) always expires before the gateway's fanout_timeout (send_after(10*1000) started after the request arrives; yuzu_gw_router.erl:139). So a forward with one silent target ends DEADLINE_EXCEEDED instead of the clean OK end the gateway gives on its own timeout (yuzu_gw_mgmt_service.erl stream_responses/3 returns ok on fanout_complete). The ADR counts 'a failed gateway forward (its 10 s deadline ...)' as send_failed, with no per-agent split. All agents of that forward, already delivered, are then counted send_failed, YuzuVizTopologyResyncBacklog's send_failed branch fires on ordinary restart waves, and the runbook row sends the operator to the gateway management plane. Convergence itself stays correct: delivered agents clear and silent ones are re-marked. Derivation: I8 base LOW. I7 (MEDIUM) governs because the forwarder's response contract is a binding design omission for slice 6. I did not apply I7's raise to HIGH: the only forgery effect left is a ResponseStore row labelled with the server-recorded __resync__ plugin, which is not Forensics-tier and has no authz consequence. If slice 6 drops the membership check, that should be re-graded under I1.
summary: The multi-agent gateway resync forward has no stated response or outcome contract. The existing single-target classifier misfires on it, and a client deadline equal to timeout_seconds turns one slow target into send_failed for every delivered agent in the forward.

trigger: An operator sets a per-OS kill switch on __resync__ (or one of its actions) for an OS that many direct-connected, diverged agents run, and leaves it set (for example during an incident).
classification_rationale: ARCH-R3-1 (d3c035f26) states that a per-OS-withheld agent is 'refused and counted send_failed ... re-issued (and refused again) once per per-agent interval while the switch stays set', and presents that as the intended signal. In the code, the per-OS withhold is applied at send time (send_to, against the session OS), but build_classified_command runs first. For each direct issuance that means the kill-switch read and then agent_service_.record_command_dispatch(...) (server/core/src/server.cpp:13242, 'written once, here ... BEFORE any frame is sent'). So every refused re-issue writes a command_execution row for a command never sent and costs two synchronous Postgres operations on the issuer thread. W withheld direct agents produce W/60 rows per second for tags, capped by the issuer's 250-1,000/s throughput. For W = 50,000 that is about 833/s, around 70 million rows a day held by the 24 h reap, plus sustained insert load on the 16-connection pool, which can feed YuzuPgPoolSaturated and #5686's presence-upsert trips. The re-issues also use up the issuer's throughput, so agents on other OSes converge more slowly, and 'deferred' rises in a way the diagnosis table attributes to Postgres overload. The cost is bounded by the issuer's rate and the reap, so this is not unbounded growth. It is a sustained, operator-triggered load on the shared Postgres pool that the ADR does not state. I5 (MEDIUM), not raised: the issuer is not on a serialised security path, and the per-OS switch is a non-default setting (E4, no change).
summary: A per-OS-withheld direct agent is rebuilt every per-agent interval. Each rebuild writes a command_execution record and a kill-switch read for a command that is never sent, so the per-OS switch costs sustained Postgres inserts and issuer throughput. The ADR does not state that cost.

trigger: A stop() arriving while an issuer pass is inside a record_command_dispatch upsert, a kill-switch read, or a steady-state (non-drain) re-claim audit write whose statement is slow or lock-blocked.
classification_rationale: CS-R3-2 (93440213c) gives the shutdown bound as '4 + 1 + 5 + 4 + 1 = 15 s', bounding the in-flight call's statement by 'the drain's SET LOCAL statement_timeout of 1 s'. That timeout applies only to drain writes. An in-flight pass call that is not a drain write runs under the pool's server-side 10 s lock_timeout and 30 s statement_timeout. server.cpp's own record_command_dispatch comment says so and reports a lock-blocked upsert measured at 10.04 s. The ADR does not put steady-state audit writes under a 1 s timeout either. The real worst case is about 4 s lease + 30 s statement + about 10 s drain, roughly 45 s. That is still inside the server's 210 s stop_grace_period in the reference composes, so no SIGKILL or row loss follows. The stated figure and the slice-6 test target ('joins within the bound') are wrong, a factual error.
summary: The 15 s shutdown bound assumes the drain's 1 s statement_timeout also bounds an in-flight pass statement. It does not, so the real bound is about 45 s (pool lock_timeout 10 s, statement_timeout 30 s).

trigger: A large re-claim audit queue (thousands of reclaim_conflict rows, e.g. a gateway restart with IP churn among retained slots in a DHCP/VPN-pool fleet) drained while Postgres is healthy but slow (S2's 300 ms added latency without failures); optionally a stop() arriving during that drain
classification_rationale: D6 (l.825-827) has the issuer write the whole queued audit backlog 'before its next pass'. A pass is cut short only by a failed write (l.832-835) or by stop (l.839, stop-time only). No per-pass row or time budget is stated, and nothing says the steady-state drain checks the stop flag between writes. Slow writes that succeed therefore hold up resync issuing for queue length x write latency: about 5 min for 1,000 rows at 300 ms, and up to about 8 h at the 100,000-row cap. During that time the pending set grows but no pass runs, so 'deferred' does not rise. The diagnosis table (l.1597) has no row for 'pending high, deferred flat, send_failed 0', and the one nearest it attributes deferral to Postgres failures. The shutdown arithmetic (l.1258-1271) counts one in-flight steady-state audit write (4 s lease), not a loop of them. A stop during a long healthy drain could exceed the 210 s TimeoutStopSec, and the resulting SIGKILL loses the rest of the queue. That contradicts 'A clean stop() never does' (l.851). The conflict counter still shows that loss gap, so this is graded I5 (issuer stall) plus I8, not I1. Base MEDIUM, E5 makes no change. Not I5(b): the issuer is not on a revocation/enforcement path, and the stall is bounded by the cap times write latency.
summary: The steady-state re-claim audit drain that runs before each resync pass has no per-pass budget and no stated stop-flag check. A large backlog against a slow but healthy pool stalls resync issuing for minutes to hours, with no diagnosis-table row for it. A stop arriving during that drain is not inside the stated ~45 s shutdown bound, which leaves the claim that a clean stop never loses a row unbacked.

trigger: Manual transaction lifecycle (BEGIN / SET LOCAL / log_in_txn / COMMIT) specified for new C++ code, where an existing owning seam (PgPool::with_txn_for) already provides the rollback-on-failure path and is the documented caller contract of log_in_txn
classification_rationale: Introduced by the CON-R3-2 / UP-R3-3 fix in this delta (ADR ~1273-1279). It writes each drain row as a hand-rolled `BEGIN`, `SET LOCAL`, `log_in_txn`, `COMMIT` on the issuer's lease and says 'a timeout rolls back only that row', but it never says who issues the ROLLBACK. The `log_in_txn` doc comment (audit_store.hpp:312-327) defines its caller contract as `pool.with_txn_for`'s `PGconn*`: on failure the caller MUST roll back, and it MUST call `count_committed(result)` after its own commit. The ADR names neither `with_txn_for` nor `count_committed`. A by-hand implementation that skips ROLLBACK on the timeout or stop path returns a mid-transaction connection to the pool. That is not a leak: `PgPool::release` (pg_pool.cpp:345-352) rolls it back or discards it with a WARN, but the cleanup then happens through a safety net, not the owner. Skipping `count_committed` silently undercounts `events_written` for every drained row. Neither path loses data (a failed row stays queued), so this is not I1-I4. Under my contract it is SHOULD rather than BLOCKING only because it is guidance in an ADR, not code. Recorder: exposure recoded by recorder from ["E-design-only: no code yet; slice 8 implements it"]; epistemic note: verified against origin/dev source (audit_store.hpp:312-333, pg_pool.cpp:345-352/393).
summary: The drain's per-row transaction is specified as hand-rolled BEGIN/SET LOCAL/log_in_txn/COMMIT without naming the owning seam (PgPool::with_txn_for, which rolls back on a false return) or the required count_committed() after commit, so the rollback owner and the success accounting are left to the implementer.

trigger: SIGTERM under a degraded Postgres pool, so several existing shutdown stages and the new resync issuer stage each run to their bound
classification_rationale: Delta hunk at ADR l.1278-1281 claims the ~45 s issuer bound is 'inside the server's 210 s stop budget'. ADR l.1256 joins the issuer sequentially in stop(). origin/dev upgrading.md ~l.5102-5129 and server-admin.md ~l.6410-6421 document a stacked worst case of ~130 s (~190 s fallback), and say an in-flight rollup can already pass 210 s; the yuzu-server.service comment says 210 s was sized for the rollup joins. A new serial stage of ~45 s brings this to ~175 s (~235 s fallback). The docs list (l.2643) cites upgrading.md but not the stacked-figure updates. Native MEDIUM (I7: docs left stale, shutdown being a non-breaking path) agrees with the derived band.
summary: The ~45 s issuer shutdown bound is presented as fitting inside the 210 s TimeoutStopSec/stop_grace_period, but it is a new sequential stage added to an already ~130 s (~190 s fallback) stacked shutdown, and the stacked figures in upgrading.md/server-admin.md are not listed for update

trigger: A pool lease that starts a fresh connection just inside its 4 s acquire deadline while the database host is slow or black-holed
classification_rationale: origin/dev pg_pool.hpp l.266-270: try_acquire_for's worst case is 'roughly timeout + connect_timeout_s' (connect_timeout_s=10). server.cpp ~l.11540-11550 (kRegistryAuditRundownBound) counts that 10 s connect for the same 4 s audit lease. The delta's arithmetic '4 + 30 + 5 + 4 + 1 = 44 s' (l.1279) and the D6 drain bound 'within about 10 s' (edited hunk l.846-850) both leave it out. Corrected: in-flight 4+10+30, drain 5 + (4+10+1), about 64 s total and about 20 s for the drain. Slices 6 and 8 size their assertions on 45 s.
summary: The shutdown arithmetic (about 45 s overall, about 10 s for the drain) omits PgPool's connect_timeout_s (10 s) that a started lease can add, which server.cpp already counts for the same 4 s audit lease

trigger: Gate 8 delta hunk at D8 'A per-OS kill switch is honoured' (UP-R3-2, 5ff330aad), checked against the ARCH-R3-2 throughput text (89126f315)
classification_rationale: The new sentence 'each refused issuance costs two Postgres operations and a record for a command never sent', and the 'W / 900 issuances per second ... rather than W / 60' figure built on it, are true only for direct-connected agents. ARCH-R3-2 (same ADR, lines ~1157-1159 and ~1283) says that for gateway agents the kill-switch read and the record_command_dispatch insert happen once per (cluster, action) forward, and that a withheld agent is 'left out of any gateway forward'. So a withheld gateway agent adds no Postgres operations of its own. The only wasted record is for a forward whose agents are all withheld after it was built, which is then skipped as empty. Also, 'rather than W / 60' assumes the 60 s tags interval; the topology interval is 5 min (W / 300). The backoff decision itself stands; only the stated cost model is wrong for gateway agents. Introduced by the UP-R3-2 hunk in this delta. Recorder: epistemic note: verified-by-reading (ADR text at 8ccdddc7e lines ~1153-1162, ~1212-1228, ~1283-1287).
summary: The cost of a per-OS refusal is stated per agent ('two Postgres operations and a record'), which contradicts the ADR's own per-forward cost for gateway agents. The W / 60 comparison holds only for the tags action.

trigger: A gateway forward with a 12 s grpc-timeout, plus router mailbox queueing (yuzu_gw_router is one gen_server shared by every fan-out on the node) or slow request arrival adding about 1 s or more between the stream's headers and the router's send_after
classification_rationale: The delta says the 12 s client deadline is 'a margin over timeout_seconds' so a silent-target forward ends on the gateway's fan-out timeout, that send_failed for the 12 s deadline is 'a transport failure before delivery', and that one slow agent 'never' turns delivered agents into send_failed. But the gateway enforces grpc-timeout itself: yuzu_grpc_stream_h:arm_deadline/2 fires at deadline_ms(12000) = 12000 - min(1000, 1200) = 11000 ms after stream init and ends the call DEADLINE_EXCEEDED. The router's 10 s timer only starts inside handle_call, after request arrival, decode and the dispatch fold. So the real margin is about 1 s minus that pre-dispatch time, not 2 s. When that margin is lost, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED arrives after the agents were already dispatched (delivered), not before delivery. Impact is a send_failed miscount that raises the 30 m ticket alert falsely; the next diverged heartbeat re-marks the agent, so the agent still converges.
summary: The 12 s vs 10 s margin ignores that the gateway answers DEADLINE_EXCEEDED itself at 11 s (yuzu_grpc_stream_h deadline_ms/1), so the effective margin is about 1 s less router queueing, and a deadline failure can follow delivery; 'before delivery' and 'never' overclaim

trigger: An agent's session ends (stream closed or error) while its __resync__ is pending in the gateway agent process
classification_rationale: The gateway's per-agent failure frames are two, not one: yuzu_gw_agent:fail_pending/1 sends {command_error, Ref, AgentId, agent_disconnected}, which streams as FAILURE / exit_code -1 / output "agent_disconnected". The existing classify_gateway_forward_response (gateway_mgmt_stub_pool.hpp:307) folds both strings into kNotConnected. The new per-agent outcome rule names only not_connected. Read literally, an agent_disconnected frame is 'an agent the stream answered for' and so counts as sent; copying the existing classifier would make it send_failed instead. The ADR says it generalises that classifier but does not say which applies. Impact is a metric miscount only; the agent's next diverged heartbeat after it reconnects re-marks it.
summary: The per-agent outcome rule covers the gateway's not_connected frame but not agent_disconnected, which today's classifier treats the same way; the classification of agent_disconnected is left ambiguous

trigger: SIGTERM to a server while the app-perf roll-up (SET LOCAL 120 s) and/or catalogue roll-up (60 s) recompute is in flight near its bound and the resync issuer is inside a pool-default statement (up to 30 s) under a degraded or slow pool, with re-claim audit rows queued
classification_rationale: The UP-R3-3 fix (cd58a504b) added 'about 45 s, inside the server's 210 s stop budget (TimeoutStopSec, the compose stop_grace_period)'. The 45 s is measured from the issuer's stop flag, but the ADR (L1256-1260) stops and joins the issuer only after the gRPC services stop, and on origin/dev ServerImpl::stop() is sequential: the roll-up joins (server.cpp stop(), app_perf_rollup_thread_.join() before agent_server_->Shutdown(5 s deadline)), then the dispatch-thread joins, then teardown. deploy/systemd/yuzu-server.service sizes 210 s for 'the worst-case sequential sum' of the roll-ups, 120 + 60 = 180 s, 'with margin', and says to raise it if a stage grows. Adding a sequential stage of about 45 s gives 180 + 5 + 45 ≈ 230 s, which is over 210 s. systemd or compose then SIGKILLs the process, which the ADR's own D6 text says loses every queued reclaim_conflict audit row uncounted. So the 'clean stop() never does' guarantee is unreachable in exactly the degraded-pool case the bound was written for. The slow pool that stretches the issuer's statement also stretches the roll-ups, so the conditions tend to occur together.
summary: The issuer's ~45 s shutdown bound is checked against the 210 s stop budget on its own. The budget is already about 180 s committed to sequential roll-up joins, and the issuer is joined after them, so the stated fit is false and a degraded-pool stop can be SIGKILLed, losing the queued re-claim audit evidence.

trigger: Compromised gateway records a signed StatusTags full set or TopologyReport from session S (sequence n); the server restarts (or the AgentHealthStore entry is pruned after 90 s, or the upstream moves replica); the gateway reattaches S under the same session id (ReattachRequest.session_id, D14) and replays the recorded payload
classification_rationale: D16 l.2059-2061 binds agent id + session id + 'a per-session sequence the server requires to increase', but the floor is held only in per-replica memory next to the D3 state map, which a restart or prune drops (D3 step 6 no_base). Reattach keeps the session id (D14 l.1698-1703, step 4 requires the stored session_id to equal the presented one), so after a restart no floor exists and an old sequence passes. A stale full set is accepted as `full`/synced with no resync, and an old TopologyReport re-claims IPs
summary: The per-session sequence floor does not survive a server restart, a prune or a replica change, but the session id does (via reattach), so an older signed payload from the same session can be replayed after a reattach and is accepted as current

trigger: Agent sends Register (direct or ProxyRegister) carrying RegisterRequest.status_tags_pb, which D16 requires to be signed with the session id bound
classification_rationale: origin/dev proto/yuzu/agent/v1/agent.proto: RegisterResponse.session_id = 1, and the server mints it (is_server_minted_session_id, gateway_service_impl.cpp:89). The agent therefore has no session id when it signs the Register full set, so D16 l.2056-2061 ('on the heartbeat and in Register ... binds ... the session id') cannot be implemented as written. An implementer who drops the binding gets a full set a gateway can replay from an earlier registration into a later Register
summary: The Register full set is required to bind a session id that only the server's response creates, so the requirement is unimplementable as stated, and the likely workaround (no binding) leaves the full set replayable across registrations

trigger: Compromised gateway with a valid certificate sends ProxyReattach for an enrolled agent whose route row is tombstoned or absent, then never forwards the challenge
classification_rationale: D14 l.1870-1872 withholds the route only at the CONNECTED re-announce. But reattach step 5 runs the shared adopt CAS (renew_leases / reclaim_tombstoned_session), which origin/dev gateway_route_store.hpp documents as re-arming the agent_routes row, and step 6 installs a dispatchable AgentSession through AgentRegistry::register_agent, both before any challenge. Dispatch is local-registry first (same header, 'read for dispatch as a FALLBACK'). 'No command but the challenge is routed' names only the __resync__ issuer (D8); no dispatch gate is named for the other paths (dispatch_confined_arms, the five cascade sites, schedule runner, policy evaluator, Guardian push, SystemReservedPush). Also: the #3425 reconnect reconciler is said to apply to a reattach (l.2428-2430), but if its containment re-dispatch is withheld during the window nothing re-fires it after verification. Teardown is stated as 'tears the stream down', which the gateway controls, not as a server-side uninstall plus tombstone
summary: The challenge-before-route rule is written for the CONNECTED re-announce only. The adopt CAS re-arms the route row and step 6 installs a dispatchable session before the challenge. No single dispatch chokepoint enforces 'no command but the challenge'. Quarantine re-application after verification and the server-side teardown are unspecified

trigger: Compromised gateway removes the new additive signature field(s) from a heartbeat or TopologyReport and alters the content. Separately, an honest gateway decodes and re-encodes HeartbeatRequest (D2 l.393) and TopologyReport (D4 l.574-575)
classification_rationale: D16 says the signature fields are 'additive proto fields' (l.2069) but never says a payload WITHOUT a signature is refused. The existing precedent is that a missing field is the benign `absent` outcome (D3 step 1), so a stripped signature plus altered bytes reads as unsigned rather than tampered. Separately, l.2059 signs 'the bytes as the agent serialized them' and l.2062 claims coalescing never breaks a signature. But the TopologyDigest is a typed sub-message the gateway decodes and re-encodes into a batch, and the gateway decodes and re-encodes TopologyReport, so the agent's serialized bytes are not what the server receives. An outer field unknown to a stale gateway *_pb.erl is also dropped
summary: Nothing requires the server to refuse an unsigned payload, so stripping the signature turns a forgery into an 'absent' or unsigned payload. The signed input is 'the agent's serialized bytes', yet the gateway decodes and re-encodes the TopologyDigest and TopologyReport, so honest relays would break the signatures

trigger: Agent signs heartbeat seq n+1 (buffered at the gateway for up to heartbeat_batch_interval_ms) and then a TopologyReport seq n+2 (forwarded unbuffered by ProxyTopology), so the report reaches the server first. Or a TopologyReport is accepted but the ack is lost, and the agent retries the same signed bytes
classification_rationale: l.2060 gives 'a per-session sequence' without saying whether heartbeats and TopologyReports share it. They travel on different paths (buffered BatchHeartbeat vs the unbuffered ProxyTopology unary, D7 'no buffering'), so with one shared space honest reordering is rejected as an 'older in-session payload'. The retry rule (D7 backoff; D2 'a failed heartbeat does not advance the base') does not say whether a retry re-signs with a new sequence. A rejection then feeds the rejected backoff (doubling to 15 min, D8 l.1362) and the three-rejects withholding rule
summary: Sequence scope and retry semantics are unspecified, so an honest reorder or a lost-ack retry can be rejected as a replay, backing off or withholding an honest agent's state

trigger: Implementer builds slice 11 from D13/D16/D14 as written
classification_rationale: Six gaps or inconsistencies a slice-11 implementer would have to guess at. (a) `yuzu_viz_topology_report_rejected_total{via,reason}` (l.1512-1513) lacks `bad_signature`, though TopologyAck gained BAD_SIGNATURE. (b) No metric or audit for challenge outcomes (verified / bad_signature / expired) or for the pending-challenge gauge, though ADR-0074 l.241 requires audit records for D5 signature refusals. (c) 'Rejected whole and changes nothing' (l.2064) contradicts D3 step 4, which clears the interval map when a heartbeat fails before step 6. (d) It is not said whether bad_signature counts toward the three-rejects withholding. (e) Verifying 'before the D3 digest check' (step 6) puts verification after decode, caps, the class check and the digest version (steps 2-5), so an altered payload can be counted `rejected` or `unverifiable` instead of `bad_signature`, and attacker bytes are parsed before they are authenticated. (f) For TopologyReport, the position relative to the OVERSIZE / UNKNOWN_SESSION checks is not stated
summary: Verification order, metric and audit coverage, and failure side effects for the signed content and the reattach challenge are incomplete or self-contradictory

trigger: Agent renews its 24-hour leaf (ADR-0074, every 12 h) mid-session, or its certificate is revoked mid-session, while it keeps sending signed heartbeats (about 3,300 per second per replica at 100k agents on a 30 s beat)
classification_rationale: l.2063 says 'verifies against the certificate it issued that agent', but an agent has overlapping certificates across a renewal. Nothing says which certificate's key verifies, whether revocation is checked per payload (is_revoked is a Postgres read that fails closed, a heavy per-heartbeat cost) or once per session, or what happens to payloads signed before a renewal. The likely failures are a false bad_signature storm at each renewal or an unbudgeted per-heartbeat revocation read Recorder derivation: impact I1 has base HIGH, so BLOCKING.
summary: The verification key selection, the revocation check and behaviour across a certificate renewal are unspecified, at a verification rate far above the result rate ADR-0074 budgets

trigger: A compromised gateway records a signed full set or TopologyReport (sequence n) under a session's current epoch, then withholds that agent's heartbeats for more than 90 s while the session stays installed, so the AgentHealthStore entry is pruned. It then replays the recorded payload under the same session and the same epoch
classification_rationale: l.2091-2094 says 'a restart, a prune or a replica change loses [the floor], but a new epoch is then required'. A prune needs no new epoch: per l.498-500 and l.1800-1803 a pruned entry with a live session only gives no_base and a __resync__.tags, and no challenge is issued. The same sentence says the floor 'is held with the session', which a prune of AgentHealthStore would not touch. The text contradicts itself. The natural implementation keeps the floor next to the D3 state map in AgentHealthStore, and under that reading an older signed payload from the same epoch passes after a prune: stale tags are accepted as `full`/synced and an old TopologyReport re-claims IPs
summary: The fix claims a prune forces a new challenge epoch, but nothing issues a challenge after a prune. Unless the floor lives in the session record, not the pruned AgentHealthStore entry, a payload from the same epoch can be replayed after a heartbeat-withholding prune

trigger: A broadcast dispatch (scope `__all__`, the legacy Broadcast forwarder, or the dispatch_scope_ladder broadcast arm) while a reattached session is `challenge_pending`
classification_rationale: l.1879-1883 names `send_to` as 'the one send every dispatch surface reaches' and puts the challenge_pending refusal there. At origin/dev, `AgentRegistry::send_to_all` (agent_registry.cpp:793) is a separate send. It snapshots every session and writes to gw_pending_ or the stream directly, without calling send_to. Its production callers are dispatch_scope_ladder.hpp:451, server.cpp:13268 and server.cpp:22847. The legacy forwarder, one of 'the five cascade sites' the ADR lists, is Broadcast-only and therefore reaches send_to_all. `send_via_directory` is covered by the `routable` refusal; send_to_all is covered by nothing
summary: The challenge_pending refusal is placed in `send_to` alone, but broadcast dispatch goes through `send_to_all`, which never calls send_to. A reattached, unverified session would still receive every broadcast command

trigger: An agent renews its leaf mid-session. ADR-0074 l.110 sets 24-hour agent certificates renewed at half-life, so this happens to every session older than about 12 h
classification_rationale: l.2117-2120 verifies against the key of the certificate the challenge was verified with. It says a renewal 're-binds at the next challenge' and defers 'how and when a renewed agent re-answers' to ADR-0074 wave 2. ADR-0074 at 6942b74a7 (D5 l.92-96, D6 l.110-113, wave-2 row) defines neither a mid-session challenge on renewal nor key continuity. In D16 the only challenges are at session start and after a reattach. Renewal every 12 h is the normal case, not an edge case. If an agent that renewed signs with its new key, every payload is `bad_signature`, which counts toward the three-rejects withholding, so honest state is withheld fleet-wide. The rule is also silent on accepting signatures after the challenge certificate's notAfter
summary: Re-binding after a renewal is deferred to an ADR-0074 that does not define it. With 12-hour renewal, a naive implementation withholds every long-lived session's state as bad_signature, and the rule says nothing about the bound certificate's expiry

trigger: An operator or reconciler quarantine/unquarantine dispatch reaches a `challenge_pending` session
classification_rationale: The quarantine routed concern (clause 3) says the protective set (`is_protective_action`) must not be refused by any enablement gate. l.1879-1885 refuses every send to a challenge_pending session except the challenge, and relies on re-firing after verification. The ADR does not say whether the protective-action exemption deliberately does not apply to this authentication gate. An implementer bound by the CATASTROPHIC clause may exempt protective actions from the refusal. That would push the stored allow-list to a session a gateway may be impersonating, while the real device is reported contained. It also leaves open what a fresh operator quarantine issued inside the window reports
summary: The challenge_pending refusal is not reconciled with the protective-action no-refusal invariant: it neither says protective actions are refused too (by decision) nor what a refused fresh quarantine reports

trigger: Any agent session that lasts longer than its bound leaf's notAfter. Under ADR-0074 D6 (24-hour leaves renewed at half-life) that is every session older than about 24 hours, with no reconnect
classification_rationale: ADR-0073 l.2133-2139 now says the agent keeps signing with the key bound at the last verified challenge, and that once that certificate's notAfter passes all state content is refused as unverified_session. It defers the re-bind to 'ADR-0074 wave 2'. The governed ADR-0074 copy (6942b74a7, D6 l.110-113, wave-2 row, open questions l.363-366) defines no mid-session re-challenge on renewal, no carry-over of the key across a renewal, and no requirement that the agent keep the superseded private key until a re-bind. Without one, StatusTags, the TopologyDigest and TopologyReport go silent fleet-wide about 24 hours into every session. They fail closed (not exploitable), but D16 presents this as a working deliverable, and that capability is not reachable
summary: The re-bind after a mid-session renewal is still deferred to an ADR-0074 that does not define it. Under the new expiry rule, every session older than about 24 hours has all signed state content refused until it reconnects

trigger: An operator issues a fresh quarantine (MCP quarantine_device, or REST POST /api/v1/quarantine) for a device whose reattached session is challenge_pending
classification_rationale: l.1893-1896 says the refused fresh quarantine is 'reported with a challenge_pending zero-reach cause, added at all five cascade sites'. At origin/dev neither quarantine path reports through those five sites. MCP quarantine_device (mcp_server.cpp ~20727-20900) shapes its answer through quarantine_response_shape (quarantine_dispatch_decision.hpp), where agents_reached==0 gives unconfirmed_retryable. REST POST /api/v1/quarantine (rest_api_v1.cpp:7570) is record-only and never dispatches. A new ConfinedDispatchOutcome cause added only at the five sites therefore never reaches the operator who issued the quarantine, so the promised cause is not delivered on the path the sentence is about. Separately, the cause cascade is a FIXED priority order duplicated at five sites (routed concern #3424/#3511), and the ADR does not say where challenge_pending ranks relative to containment_unreadable, os_gate_unreadable and quarantined. Each site may then rank it differently: the drift that routed concern exists to prevent
summary: The challenge_pending zero-reach cause is said to report a refused fresh quarantine, but quarantine reports through quarantine_response_shape (MCP) or does not dispatch at all (REST), not through the five cascade sites. The cause's rank in the fixed cascade is also unstated

trigger: Clean stop() (SIGTERM) while agents keep sending heartbeats, and a re-claim conflict (D6) happens after the issuer has finished its stop-time drain and exited. That is up to 64 s after the flag, while gRPC ingestion stays live until agent_server_->Shutdown. On origin/dev that Shutdown runs only after the --shutdown-drain-seconds grace and the roll-up joins (up to 180 s).
classification_rationale: f5d514398 moved the issuer's stop flag to the start of stop(), so its drain and exit now run alongside the roll-up joins. Ingestion is still live then (origin/dev stop(): draining_ and the grace, then the roll-up joins, then agent_server_->Shutdown). The heartbeat path's re-claim conflict queues its topology.push.rejected row for the issuer (D6, L826-829). A row queued after the issuer's stop-time drain is never written, never counted and never WARN-logged. The fix covers resync marks only ('a mark made after the flag is set is dropped', L1272). Meanwhile L859-861 still says 'A clean stop() never does' lose queued rows, and L865-866 says the evidence chain records a refused re-claim except in the listed loss cases. This is an unlisted, silent loss of an audit evidence row on a clean stop.
summary: With the issuer stopped early (the ARCH-R4-1 fix), D6 re-claim audit rows queued by the still-live heartbeat path after the issuer's stop-time drain are lost silently. That contradicts the ADR's claim that a clean stop() loses no queued row.

trigger: An implementer builds slice 11's post-reattach challenge. The server must push a challenge down an established, possibly gateway-proxied Subscribe stream, and take the agent's answer back on both the direct and gateway ingress paths.
classification_rationale: D14 says the server 'sends a signed session-start challenge down the existing stream' and that 'the challenge push is the one exempt send'. Slice 11 adds 'answering a session-start challenge arriving mid-stream'. Neither the ADR nor ADR-0074 at 6942b74a7 names the wire carrier. ADR-0074 D5 (L92) describes the challenge only as happening 'at the start of every session'. Slice 11's proto bullet lists only the envelope fields. If the carrier is a reserved command name like __resync__, it falls under several standing rules. CommandDedupStore: dedup is the safe default for reserved names, and __guard__ is the only bypass. notify_exec_tracker prefix skipping. The command_execution provenance record and ~unverified labelling (#4990 clause 7). The ExecuteGate consteval sweep. If it is a new message, it is a proto addition the gateway must pass through, and both proto copies and *_pb.erl must carry it. Either way, which send function exempts it is a chokepoint decision. The routed-concern rows warn against a second send path. And an unspecified answer-ingest path is where a gateway could forge or mis-route the answer.
summary: The post-reattach challenge and its answer have no specified wire carrier, ingest path or exempt send primitive. The design leaves open whether they are a reserved command (with dedup, exec-tracker, provenance and ExecuteGate consequences) or new stream messages (a proto change not in slice 11's proto list).

trigger: A TopologyReport is refused as replayed or unverified_session. Examples: one sent between a reattach and its challenge verifying, or one sent after the bound certificate's notAfter.
classification_rationale: The metric reason set (L1515-1517) gains bad_signature, replayed and unverified_session for yuzu_viz_topology_report_rejected_total. But the wire contract TopologyAck.reject_reason (L900) gains only BAD_SIGNATURE, so the server has no enum value to send for the other two. The agent's retry rule (D7, L792: a full floor after IP_CONFLICT, exponential back-off otherwise) and the 'After a rejected report' digest-recording and resync-suppression rule (L787-794) are not stated for any of the three new reasons. If an implementer maps unverified_session to UNKNOWN_SESSION or BAD_SIGNATURE, the agent backs off exponentially right after its challenge verifies. A BAD_SIGNATURE mapping also feeds the three-rejects withholding, which D16 says expiry must never do.
summary: TopologyAck.reject_reason gains only BAD_SIGNATURE, while the server distinguishes replayed and unverified_session. The agent's retry behaviour and the server's rejected-digest recording are unspecified for all three wave-2 reasons.

adjudication_rationale: Re-derived: impact I3 has base band HIGH, so the derived band is BLOCKING (reporter mapped SHOULD).
trigger: Concurrent handling of one session's state: two gateway ProxyHeartbeat or ProxyTopology RPCs for the same session on different gRPC threads; or the challenge answer arriving as the --reattach-challenge-timeout expiry fires; or a post-reattach challenge verifying (new epoch) while an in-flight payload signed under the old epoch is between signature verification and floor advance
classification_rationale: The delta adds new mutable post-publication AgentSession state: challenge_pending, the verified challenge epoch, the bound verification key, and two per-kind sequence floors. Each is read by send_to/send_to_all (under stream_mu), the routable predicate, the heartbeat path and the topology path. The ADR names no lock for any of it, and does not require the AgentSession publication-discipline comment in agent_registry.hpp to be amended. That comment confines post-publication writes to a closed list of fields under stream_mu or mu_. As written an implementer can (a) check the floor and advance it in separate critical sections, so two copies of one signed payload both pass; (b) let the challenge-verify path and the expiry path both win, so a verified session gets uninstalled and tombstoned, or an expired one has challenge_pending cleared and its route republished, which wedges the route/session state machine; (c) advance a floor under epoch E after epoch E+1 is installed. Every other mechanism in this ADR (apply's mu_ read/copy/commit, pushed_mu_, the issuer in-flight table) states its lock and its single-winner rule; D14/D16 do not. Severity is SHOULD rather than BLOCKING only because this is design guidance, not code.
summary: D14/D16 add mutable session-record state (challenge_pending, verified epoch, bound key, per-kind floors) without naming its lock, the atomic check-and-advance of the sequence floor, or the single-winner resolution of the challenge (verified vs bad_signature vs expired).

trigger: A state payload being verified on a gRPC thread while the session is uninstalled (challenge failure or expiry teardown, supersession) or re-bound by a renewal challenge
classification_rationale: D16 'key' says the server verifies against the key of the certificate the session's challenge was verified with, so each session record now holds an OpenSSL public-key object (or the cert it is derived from). The ADR does not say who owns that object or how a verifier holds it across verification. Verification must run outside the registry and session locks: at N/30 s per replica it is about 3,300 verifies per second at N = 100,000, and under mu_ it would serialise every dispatch. So the verifier needs an owning reference that survives a concurrent uninstall or re-bind. A raw EVP_PKEY* or X509* borrowed from the session is a use-after-free when teardown or a re-bind frees it mid-verify; reparsing peer_cert_pem per payload is wasteful. This is borrowed-data escape on my contract's list; it is SHOULD because it is design guidance.
summary: The bound verification key's owner type and lifetime are unspecified: the per-payload verify must run outside the locks, which needs an owned refcounted reference, not a raw EVP_PKEY*/X509* borrowed from the session record.

trigger: A reattached session whose agent never answers the challenge; --reattach-challenge-timeout (30 s) must fire with no inbound event to drive it
classification_rationale: D14 requires the server to uninstall the session and tombstone its route row itself when no answer arrives within the expiry ('it does not rely on the gateway closing the stream'). The expiry therefore needs a server-side timer or sweep, but the ADR names no thread that owns it, no stop/join point in stop()/~ServerImpl relative to the registry and the route store it writes, and no Postgres lease budget for the tombstone write. Every other background actor in this ADR (the issuer, the roll-up joins) states its owner, stop flag, join order and shutdown bound. An implementer could add a detached timer per challenge, or a new unjoined thread that outlives the registry. Both are ambiguously-owned thread cases on my contract's list; SHOULD because this is design guidance.
summary: The challenge-expiry teardown names no owning thread or sweep, no stop/join position in stop()/~ServerImpl, and no lease budget for its tombstone write.

trigger: A server restart with N gateway agents: every reattach (up to --reattach-rate, default 2000/s per replica) sends a post-reattach challenge to a gateway session. The ADR places that push as 'the one exempt send' inside send_to. On origin/dev, send_to queues a gateway session's command on gw_pending_, and forward_gateway_pending (server.cpp ~l.13854-13990) starts one detached std::thread per command, with a 300 s SendCommand deadline and up to three retries with exponential sleeps; the thread is never joined (#3279).
classification_rationale: The ADR does not say which forwarding path the challenge (and the containment re-dispatch that follows verification) takes for a gateway session. Every reattached session is a gateway session, and the default path is the one D8 itself rejects for resyncs at a similar rate ('would turn a resync wave into unbounded thread growth, starve command and containment forwarding on the same path, and make the issuer's bounded shutdown false'). A challenge cannot share a multi-agent forward, because each one is signed and bound to its agent. So at 2000/s with a slow or blackholed gateway management plane, threads grow without bound on the path that also carries containment forwarding. That makes it I5 case (b), which raises the band to HIGH. A secondary point: a 300 s, 3-retry forward can deliver a challenge long after its 30 s expiry, which is wasted work.
summary: The post-reattach challenge push has no specified forwarding path. Its default for gateway sessions (gw_pending_ → forward_gateway_pending: one detached thread per command, held for up to 300 s) multiplies by --reattach-rate during a restart storm. That is the unbounded-thread, containment-starving hazard D8 rejects for __resync__.

adjudication_rationale: Re-derived: impact I3 has base band HIGH, so the derived band is BLOCKING (reporter mapped SHOULD).
trigger: A post-reattach challenge expires (no answer within 30 s, for example because the forward or agent is slow during a restart storm) or fails to verify. The server uninstalls the session and tombstones the route row, but the AgentRegistrationStore record survives. The agent's next heartbeat makes the server report the session as unknown, the gateway replays by ids (ProxyReattach), and D14 states that a tombstoned row is reclaimed under any well-formed session id.
classification_rationale: Line ~1908 says that after a failure or expiry 'the agent registers again through the full path'. The mechanism the ADR describes yields another reattach and another challenge, not a full Register, because the record is still present and the gateway only closes the stream on NO_RECORD. Under storm overload, every expiry therefore feeds another reattach plus challenge, throttled only by --reattach-rate and with no per-agent backoff. That is a metastable retry loop that can stop the restart wave converging. For a persistently bad signature it is an endless loop of reattach and teardown.
summary: Challenge failure or expiry tombstones the route but not the registration record, so it leads back into reattach and a new challenge rather than the stated full Register. Under load this becomes a retry loop with no backoff.

trigger: Any registration from wave 2: a gateway restart (about 1,700 Register/s for 100,000 agents within ADR-0074 D14's 60 s target), an agent reconnect, or the NO_RECORD path. Register's status_tags_pb is now ignored, and state is only accepted after the challenge verifies plus a __resync__.tags round trip.
classification_rationale: Several statements were not updated for the decision. D8 'Loss' (l.~1367) says 'its Register carries the full set anyway', which is false from wave 2. *Fleet-gauge semantics* (l.~1654) presents no_base and absent state gauges as a server-restart consequence only. From wave 2, every gateway restart and every reconnect also leaves an agent's state-derived gauges absent until challenge, resync issuance and the next heartbeat. A gateway reconnect storm used to cost zero resyncs and now issues N, at the real issuer throughput D8 gives (100-400 s for direct agents, about 500 s behind a single cluster). D16's 'the issuer's rate already budgets for a restart (D8)' covers the size of the rate but not this new, recurring, operator-visible gap. Each Register also still carries about 4 KB that the server ignores.
summary: From wave 2 every registration, not only a server restart, starts with no state map and needs a resync. D8 'Loss' still says Register carries the full set, and the operator-visible consequences describe the gap only after a server restart.

trigger: Steady state at N = 100,000 per replica, about 3,300 signed heartbeats per second, all verified inline before decode (D16 'order'), including on the gateway BatchHeartbeat path. Under a backlog flush, one BatchHeartbeat chunk is up to 3 MiB (yuzu_gw_heartbeat_buffer.erl ?MAX_CHUNKS_PER_FLUSH 8), which is thousands of heartbeats, each verified serially on one handler thread against the gateway's 5 s call timeout. The per-kind floors live in the AgentRegistry session record.
classification_rationale: The ADR carefully keeps Postgres and sends off the BatchHeartbeat path so that 'a slow pool cannot push a batch past the timeout'. It does not apply the same discipline to the new per-heartbeat CPU cost. It states no bound on verifications per batch, no parallelism, and no rule that verification runs outside the AgentRegistry lock: read key, epoch and floor under the lock, verify outside, then advance the floor by compare-and-set. It also does not say that the parsed verification key and notAfter are cached in the session record, rather than looked up or parsed from the certificate per payload. A timed-out batch is resent by the gateway, which amplifies load. The S1 assertions (BatchHeartbeat p99 under 2 s, no batch retried on timeout, breaker not tripped) are owned by slices 6/7b, before slice 11 adds verification and the challenge, and slice 11's tests do not re-run S1.
summary: Heartbeat-rate signature verification is placed inline on BatchHeartbeat with no per-batch CPU bound against the 5 s timeout, no lock rule for the registry-held floors, and no key cache. The restart-storm chaos run that would catch this (S1) is not re-run once slice 11 lands.

trigger: The D8 'Combined Postgres rate after a server restart' and D14 storm step 1, read after the wave-2 challenge is added
classification_rationale: Both places still give 'four Postgres operations per reattach' and the derived figure of about 12,400 operations per second per replica. From wave 2 each reattach also clears challenge_pending on the route row after verification, which is at least one more route write. If the challenge is built through build_classified_command like every other dispatch, it also adds a kill-switch read and a command_execution record. That is 5-7 operations per reattach, or 2,000-6,000 more operations per second at the default --reattach-rate, against a pool size of 16. The figure is marked unmeasured, but the stated count is now wrong.
summary: The per-reattach Postgres cost (four operations, about 12,400/s combined) does not include the wave-2 challenge_pending clear or the challenge's own dispatch record and kill-switch read.

trigger: A reattached session whose challenge does not verify: a bad signature, or no answer within --reattach-challenge-timeout. Examples: the CONNECTED re-announce was dropped by the gateway's cast, so the challenge could not be routed; the mgmt plane to the cluster is down; or the leaf is past notAfter. Meanwhile the agent's Subscribe stream to the gateway stays up.
classification_rationale: D14 says that on failure the server uninstalls the session and tombstones its route row, and that 'the agent registers again through the full path'. Nothing in the design tells the gateway or the agent to do that. The gateway still holds the session and answers the agent's heartbeats locally (D4). On the next BatchHeartbeat the server lists the session id in unknown_session_ids. The gateway's targeted replay, which D14 keeps unchanged, then sends ProxyReattach with the same ids. Step 4 passes, because the record's stored session_id still matches. Step 5 reclaims the tombstoned row 'under any well-formed session id' (D14's own words). The session is installed challenge_pending again and challenged again. So the session cycles reattach, challenge, expire, teardown, unknown, reattach, about every 30-40 s and indefinitely. The gateway only disconnects on NO_RECORD, NOT_ENROLLED, SUPERSEDED or MALFORMED_SESSION, and none of those is produced. Each failure writes an agent.reattach.challenge audit row, so audit volume per stuck agent is unbounded. The cycle also spends --reattach-rate tokens that other agents' reattaches need. The agent never reaches the full Register that the ADR promises, and it stays unroutable (containment included) for as long as the loop runs. This wedges a state machine and puts unbounded writes on the audit path (I5 raised to HIGH under (b) and (c)).
summary: After a challenge failure, nothing makes the agent re-register: the gateway sees the session in unknown_session_ids and reattaches it again, the tombstoned row is reclaimed, and the reattach/challenge/teardown cycle (one audit row per failure) never ends

trigger: Any reattach that arrives through a gateway, which in practice is every reattach, since reattach is a gateway-upstream RPC
classification_rationale: D14 says the challenge goes 'down the existing stream' and that 'steps 5 and 6 still run, so the server can send the challenge'. For a gateway session the server holds no stream. The only path from the server to the agent is send_to's gw_pending_ branch, then forward_gateway_pending, then ManagementService.SendCommand. That branch needs session->gateway_node and cluster_id, and those are set only by the CONNECTED re-announce, which the gateway casts and drops with no retry when its circuit is open or at least 10 notifies are in flight. That is exactly the state during a reattach storm. So the challenge cannot be sent at step 6, and the expiry timer has to start when the challenge is actually sent. The ADR does not cover: (a) that the send waits for CONNECTED, and what happens when CONNECTED never arrives; (b) that forward_gateway_pending sends timeout_seconds 300, a 300 s deadline and three retries, which leaves the gateway router's fan-out state and a detached server thread alive for about 300 s after the 30 s expiry, once per loop iteration of GW-R5-1 (the same lesson D8 already applied to __resync__); (c) that the answer comes back on the SendCommandResponse stream to process_gateway_response, and must be routed to the verifier there rather than ingested or exec-tracked as an ordinary command response; (d) that whatever fields carry the challenge and its answer on CommandRequest/CommandResponse must be in the gateway's vendored agent.proto copies (flat and nested), which management.proto and gateway.proto embed. gpb drops unknown fields when it decodes and re-encodes (the ForwardGuardianRequest comment documents this hazard for plugin/action/payload). Slice 11's proto bullet names only 'the additive envelope fields'. ADR-0074 at 6942b74a7 does not define a transport for the per-session challenge either.
summary: How the post-reattach challenge reaches a gateway-attached agent is not specified, and 'down the existing stream' is wrong. In practice it is a mgmt-plane SendCommand that cannot be sent before the droppable CONNECTED re-announce, that uses 300 s forward timeouts, whose answer returns on the forward's response stream, and whose fields gpb will strip unless the gateway's vendored protos carry them

caused_by: SEC-2 owner decision (D16 signed state content)
trigger: A wave-2 agent (a buggy build, or a compromised agent with a valid certificate) sends a heartbeat whose signed envelope field is large. The listener allows up to 4 MiB per message.
classification_rationale: D4 makes the gateway's oversize drop, its buffer byte cap and its chunk packing depend on yuzu_gw_heartbeat_buffer:estimate_bytes/1 'counting the new fields (slice 3)'. estimate_bytes/1 adds up named map keys only (l.687-690 at origin/dev). D16 adds a new heartbeat bytes field, the envelope, and deprecates the typed fields it replaces, but neither D4 nor slice 11 says estimate_bytes must count it. If it does not, the per-heartbeat oversize drop never fires on the payload that actually carries state. The buffer's byte cap stops bounding gateway memory. And chunks packed to ?CHUNK_BYTES by estimate can exceed the upstream message limit, failing a whole BatchHeartbeat chunk and with it the liveness of every other session in that chunk. D4's 'No parsing' list and slice 11's gateway bullet do not mention the heartbeat envelope at all. Two smaller gaps on ReportTopology: the gateway admits the report by its session, so session_id must stay an unsigned top-level field outside the envelope; and the route's 2 MiB message cap now has to hold a body of up to 2 MiB plus the envelope's binding and signature overhead, so a near-cap body is refused at the gateway's frame header (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED) instead of reaching the server as OVERSIZE.
summary: The new heartbeat envelope field is not added to the gateway's estimate_bytes/1, which adds up named fields only, so the oversize drop, buffer byte cap and chunk packing stop bounding the state payload. ReportTopology's outer session_id and its message cap versus body-plus-envelope are also unstated

trigger: A session for agent A on a challenge_pending reattach loses the single-winner transition to failed/expired (bad or missing answer). Before the off-lock uninstall and tombstone lease completes (this may be delayed by Postgres lease wait), an operator broadcast, schedule run, policy dispatch or system-reserved push calls send_to / send_to_all for A.
classification_rationale: The authentication gate is stated as refusing a `challenge_pending` session (l.1942-1943, 'through one shared predicate'). The new locking clause (l.1964-1967) moves the session state from `pending` to `failed` or `expired` under stream_mu, and puts the uninstall, tombstone and record write on a bounded lease outside every registry lock (l.1985-1986). The ADR never says the shared predicate refuses `failed` and `expired`, or that the in-memory uninstall is atomic with the transition. An implementation that keys the predicate on the pending state, which is the literal reading, opens a window in which a session that just FAILED authentication is sendable. That session may belong to a gateway impersonating the device. This is a fail-open on the gate the owner decided must hold. I record native HIGH; the E2 raise would derive CRITICAL, and the gate outcome is BLOCKING either way.
summary: The challenge_pending send predicate is not stated to be fail-closed on every non-verified state. After the transition to failed or expired, and before the off-lock uninstall, an unauthenticated session may receive commands.

trigger: Agent A has an honest `expired` (or `degraded`) challenge failure through gateway G1, which writes the agent's one audit row. Within the next 10 min, a compromised gateway G2 reattaches A's session and returns a forged answer (`bad_signature`).
classification_rationale: The new rule writes an `agent.reattach.challenge` audit row 'at most once per agent per 10 min; later failures are counted only' (l.1990-1992), with the key being the agent alone. The forged answer, which is the attack this challenge exists to detect, therefore produces no audit row. It appears only on an unlabelled counter. YuzuStateSignatureRefused's runbook (l.1655-1657) tells the responder that the audit rows 'name the agent and the gateway; check that gateway first', so the responder would investigate G1, the honest gateway. The reconnect-storm justification fits `expired` and `degraded`, which are expected in bulk. It does not fit `bad_signature`, which honest agents never produce. The audit control does not hold for the security event, and the shipped runbook points at the wrong actor.
summary: The per-agent 10-minute audit suppression lets an honest expired row mask a later forged-answer (bad_signature) row. The alert runbook then sends the responder to the wrong gateway.

trigger: Session S's challenge fails, and the agent then completes a fresh full Register (new session S2: record session_id = S2, route row renewed for S2) before the off-lock failure lease runs the tombstone and record write for S.
classification_rationale: The new failure clause (l.1973-1976) clears 'the AgentRegistrationStore record's session_id' and tombstones the route row 'in the same transaction'. The write runs later on a bounded lease (l.1985). The ADR does not state that either write is conditional on the stored session still being S. Written unconditionally, it clears S2's record and tombstones S2's live route. A healthy agent then becomes unroutable (zero reach) and receives NO_RECORD on its gateway's next replay, so it is forced to re-register. This is availability for an honest agent, with no escalation, so the derived band is MEDIUM.
summary: The record session_id clear and the route tombstone on challenge failure are not stated to be guarded on the failed session's id, so they can clobber a newer session.

trigger: An implementer or alert author reads the D13 metric inventory (docs/adr/0073-liveness-heartbeat-tag-deltas-topology-rpc.md line ~1534) for the `yuzu_server_reattach_challenge_total` outcome set and gets a three-value set. D14 now defines five.
classification_rationale: The ADR contradicts itself: D13 lists `verified|bad_signature|expired`; the fix's D14 text lists `verified|bad_signature|expired|degraded|send_failed`. Both are wording of the same metric contract, so the inconsistency is internal to the ADR.
summary: The D13 `yuzu_server_reattach_challenge_total{outcome}` list was not updated for the `degraded` and `send_failed` outcomes the fix added in D14. The new `YuzuStateSignatureRefused` rule matches only `bad_signature|expired`, and nothing in D13 says whether `degraded` and `send_failed` are deliberately left out of it.
