trigger: An implementer of slice 11 reads both ADR clauses that define how a challenge forward that never completes is handled. Or the replica's challenge-forward slots (--reattach-challenge-concurrency, default 256) are full during a post-restart reattach wave, so challenges cannot start before their expiry.
classification_rationale: The fix's new clause (l.1995-1999) says a failed challenge forward resolves at once as `send_failed` and is handled like `degraded`: uninstalled with the record kept, because nothing was learned about the agent. The forwarding clause (l.1934-1935) was left as it was: 'a challenge that cannot start before its expiry is counted `send_failed` and resolved as `expired`'. Under the failure clause, `expired` clears the record and tombstones the route, which forces the agent through a full re-register. So one counter value has two opposite dispositions, and it is unclear whether such a challenge is counted once or twice. The rationale given for keeping the record ('nothing was learned about the agent') applies just as much to a challenge that never started. If the case is counted `expired`, a capacity overload trips YuzuStateSignatureRefused (`expired` > 0). That alert's responder text tells the operator to suspect a gateway, which is the misdirection the round-5d fix removed for `send_failed`. Neither reading admits an unverified session, because the predicate admits only `verified`. The impact is therefore a doc contradiction plus a possible misfire of the security alert, not a fail-open.
summary: The forwarding clause still says a challenge that cannot start before its expiry is 'counted `send_failed` and resolved as `expired`' (record cleared). That contradicts the new rule that `send_failed` is handled like `degraded` (record kept), and it would let a server-side concurrency shortage fire the gateway-forgery alert.

classification_rationale: Fixed in dd7eb5953 (one-line contradiction removed; SHOULD, no further Gate 2 iteration required: Gate 2 PASS at 5e; reconfirmed by the Gate 3 re-review over the same text).

trigger: A gateway agent reattaches and the gateway's CONNECTED re-announce for it is dropped. The re-announce is a cast, which the ADR itself says 'the gateway casts and may drop', and drops are likeliest under a reattach wave. So the challenge is never sent, and the session sits challenge_pending with no send time.
classification_rationale: D14 says 'the expiry starts at the send' and 'a session whose CONNECTED never arrives within the expiry is counted expired'. For an unsent challenge there is no send, so the deadline the issuer's sweep compares against ('challenge_pending sessions past their deadline') is undefined. The ADR also classes a lost management-plane cast as `expired`, while it classes the equivalent management-plane failures (forward failed, not_connected, agent_disconnected, concurrency saturation) as `send_failed`, 'because nothing was learned about the agent'. That has two effects. (1) It takes the agent-fault failure path, which clears the registration record's session_id and forces a full Register, instead of the degraded/send_failed path, which keeps the record. (2) `expired` is in YuzuStateSignatureRefused, so a benign gateway drop raises the 'a gateway altered content' ticket. That contradicts the stated reason for leaving send_failed and degraded out of the rule, and it contradicts the S1/S2 slice-11 assertion that `expired` stays at 0 for honest agents.
summary: A session whose CONNECTED re-announce never arrives has no defined expiry deadline, because the expiry starts at a send that never happens. It is also counted `expired`, an agent-fault outcome that clears the registration record and raises the forgery ticket, although nothing was learned about the agent.

adjudication_rationale: Reclassified wording -> truth-contradiction: the text as written admits a lock-order inversion against origin/dev (I5), which is a truth finding, not wording.
trigger: An implementer reads D14 locking, 'A winning failed or expired transition removes the session from the registry's sendable set in the same critical section', taken under the session's stream_mu, as erasing the session from the registry's session map, which is guarded by AgentRegistry::mu_.
classification_rationale: The phrase 'the registry's sendable set' is not defined anywhere in the ADR. On origin/dev the registry's lock order is mu_ then stream_mu (agent_registry.cpp set_stream ~l.251 and the send paths). Taking mu_ while holding stream_mu inverts that order and can deadlock the registry, which every dispatch and registration path shares. The ADR's own fail-closed predicate already refuses `failed` and `expired`, so the state write under stream_mu is enough to leave the sendable set. Read literally, though, the text asks for a cross-lock erase. The slice-11 TSan race test would probably flag an inversion, which keeps this at SHOULD.
summary: 'Removes the session from the registry's sendable set in the same critical section' (under stream_mu) is undefined. Read as a map erase, it inverts origin/dev's mu_ -> stream_mu lock order.

trigger: Wave 2 is implemented from both ADRs. ADR-0074 D5 (adr-0074-at-6942b74a7.md l.92) defines the challenge only as 'at the start of every session'. ADR-0073 D14 now names `__session__.challenge` as the carrier for 'the same challenge D5 issues at the start of every session', but only for the post-reattach case.
classification_rationale: Neither ADR says whether the challenge at the start of a full Register also travels as `__session__.challenge`. Neither does ADR-0074 record that a challenge can arrive mid-stream after a reattach. If ADR-0074's implementer picks a different session-start carrier (for example a Register/Subscribe message field), there are two carriers for one primitive, with two ingest drops and two exemption paths. That is the second-copy drift the dispatch chokepoint rows warn against. Today D14's 'same challenge' claim is asserted but not anchored in ADR-0074.
summary: The post-reattach challenge carrier is fixed in ADR-0073, but ADR-0074 D5 neither names the session-start carrier nor acknowledges the mid-stream post-reattach challenge, so the two ADRs can diverge onto two carriers.

adjudication_rationale: Re-derived: impact I3 has base band HIGH, so the derived band is BLOCKING (reporter mapped SHOULD).
caused_by: 2701b4302 (CS-R5-1..3 / GW-R5 fix delta, forwarding bullet), 7faf167fc / dd7eb5953 (concurrency and send_failed wording)
trigger: A stop() with challenge forwards still in flight, or an issuer pass blocked in a Postgres call (up to 4+10+30 s per D8) while honest challenge answers are already waiting on the async completion queue
classification_rationale: The new forwarding bullet says the challenge 'goes through the issuer-owned forwarder (D8: the in-flight table, TryCancel at stop, joined before gw_mgmt_pool_)', but in the same sentence it describes a different mechanism: up to 256 forwards 'driven by the gRPC async client on the issuer's thread rather than a thread per forward'. D8's forwarder is the opposite design. It is a bounded set of at most 8 threads, each owning a synchronous ClientContext, and D8's lifetime proof depends on that: the entry is removed under the in-flight mutex before the context is destroyed, and TryCancel is called only while holding that mutex. That proof does not carry over to the async API. Each call's ClientContext, ClientAsyncReader and response buffer must outlive the call's final CQ tag, not just the TryCancel. The CompletionQueue must be Shutdown() and drained with Next() until it returns false before it is destroyed, and before the channels in gw_mgmt_pool_ are destroyed. Destroying a CQ that still has pending tags is a gRPC assertion or a use-after-free. The ADR names none of these: no CQ owner, no per-call tag owner, no drain point in stop() relative to the issuer join and gw_mgmt_pool_. Also, the CQ is polled on the same thread that runs the expiry sweep and D8's blocking Postgres calls. If a pass sweeps before draining the CQ, or stalls in a lease longer than the 30 s expiry, an honest answer already sitting in the queue is resolved as `expired`. That clears the registration record (forcing a full re-register) and fires YuzuStateSignatureRefused, i.e. an honest agent is reported as a challenge failure. This is borrowed-lifetime ambiguity and ambiguous thread/queue ownership, both on my blocking contract. It is SHOULD because it is design guidance, not code.
summary: The challenge forwarder is described both as D8's thread-per-forward in-flight table and as an async-CQ client on the issuer's thread. The async variant's CompletionQueue, per-call ClientContext/reader/tag ownership, shutdown drain order and its polling relative to the expiry sweep are unspecified.

caused_by: 7faf167fc (SEC-R5D-R5-01..03: failed transition leaves the sendable set in the same critical section)
trigger: An implementer reading 'A winning failed or expired transition removes the session from the registry's sendable set in the same critical section' as erasing the session from AgentRegistry::agents_ (under mu_) while already holding the session's stream_mu, concurrently with set_stream/send_to_all, which take mu_ and then stream_mu
classification_rationale: The locking bullet puts the transition under the session's stream_mu and says the winning failed or expired transition 'removes the session from the registry's sendable set in the same critical section'. On origin/dev the registry's lock order is mu_ then stream_mu: agent_registry.cpp set_stream takes lock(mu_) and then it->second->stream_mu, and send_to_all locks each snapshot session's stream_mu. Erasing the session from agents_ needs mu_, so doing it inside a stream_mu critical section inverts that order and can deadlock against set_stream. The requirement can be met without mu_: the fail-closed predicate (added in 7faf167fc) admits only `verified`, so writing failed/expired under stream_mu already takes the session out of the sendable set. The registry erase can then happen afterwards with the normal order. The ADR does not say which reading is meant and states no lock order, so the deadlock-prone reading is open to an implementer. This is SHOULD because it is design guidance.
summary: 'Removes the session from the registry's sendable set in the same critical section' under stream_mu can be read as erasing from agents_ under mu_ while holding stream_mu, which inverts the registry's established mu_ -> stream_mu order.

caused_by: PERF-R5-1 fix (2701b4302) with the 7faf167fc/dd7eb5953 send_failed handling
trigger: Server restart with N = 100,000 agents spread over ten or more gateways: reattaches arrive at the --reattach-rate cap of 2000/s (D14 storm step 1). Each reattach queues a __session__.challenge. Per D14 *carrier*, the challenge is built with build_classified_command on the issuer's single thread, which means two synchronous Postgres operations per challenge (kill-switch read, record insert). D8 bounds that thread at about 250-1,000 issuances/s. The same thread also issues the per-registration tag resyncs that wave 2 adds. The ADR also says each challenge forward is held open until the agent's signed answer comes back on its SendCommandResponse stream, so --reattach-challenge-concurrency 256 sustains 256 / round-trip per second (about 2,560/s at 100 ms, 256/s at 1 s).
classification_rationale: The ADR now says that 'a challenge that cannot start before its expiry resolves send_failed and is handled ... uninstalled, the record kept', and that the agent may reattach again. It never compares the challenge start rate with the reattach arrival rate. By D8's own figures the start rate (at most about 250-1,000/s, shared with tag resyncs) is below the 2000/s default --reattach-rate. During every restart storm, a share of honest agents therefore waits past the 30 s expiry, is torn down as send_failed and reattaches again. Each cycle repeats the four reattach operations plus the route writes, keeps the agent unroutable for longer (commands get the challenge_pending zero-reach cause), and does no useful work. The system still converges at the challenge service rate, so this is wasted capacity and a slower restart, not a wedge (I8). It is also I6 because the slice-11 S1 re-run asserts only expired = 0 and a pending-gauge bound of min(--reattach-rate × expiry, held sessions). Overflow is labelled send_failed, not expired, so the assertion passes while the waste happens. Only the concurrency-saturation test looks at send_failed, and it treats it as expected. The --reattach-challenge-concurrency default of 256 is not derived from --reattach-rate and the challenge round trip.
summary: The challenge start rate (issuer thread, two synchronous Postgres operations each; 256 forwards held for the agent's round trip) is below the 2000/s reattach rate it must keep up with. Overflow becomes send_failed with the record kept and another reattach, which churns honest agents through repeated reattaches during every restart storm. S1's 'expired = 0' assertion cannot catch it because overflow is counted send_failed.

adjudication_rationale: Re-derived: impact I3 has base band HIGH, so the derived band is BLOCKING (reporter mapped SHOULD).
caused_by: GW-R5-2 fix in 2701b4302 (premise taken from GW-R5-2's own incorrect 'casts and drops' description)
trigger: A reattach whose CONNECTED re-announce reaches the server more than --reattach-challenge-timeout (30 s) after the reattach. On origin/dev this is ordinary. (a) Reattach storm: yuzu_gw_upstream holds the notification in yuzu_gw_notify_queue and drains it FIFO at most ?MAX_NOTIFY_INFLIGHT (10) at a time, so tens of thousands of CONNECTEDs behind one another take minutes. (b) Breaker open or half_open: the entry is held with no time limit. (c) The server answers acknowledged=false, for example connected_unverified while the route directory read is degraded: the resend backoff is decorrelated jitter between 1 s and 60 s, averaging about 34 s. (d) A CONNECTED evicted or refused at a full store waits for a full registration replay.
classification_rationale: D14 carrier (line ~1924) says the CONNECTED re-announce is one 'which the gateway casts and may drop'. At origin/dev it is held, not dropped (#4632/#5695, yuzu_gw_upstream.erl l.38-70 and l.160-240). It is delayed by the 10-in-flight drain, by the breaker and by the unacked-resend backoff, and is lost only by eviction or a full store, either of which arms a registration replay. This wording came from my own GW-R5-2 and is wrong. From that false premise, D14 says 'a session whose CONNECTED never arrives within the expiry is counted expired'. expired is the agent-fault outcome: it clears the registration record, so the next replay gets NO_RECORD and closes the stream. It also feeds YuzuStateSignatureRefused, and audit rows are written. So an honest agent whose CONNECTED was only delayed by its own gateway's notify queue is forced into a full Register. That happens fleet-wide in exactly the post-restart reattach storm that reattach exists to absorb, turning it into a registration storm. It contradicts the S1/S2 slice-11 assertion that expired is 0 for honest agents, and the alert test 'quiet through an expected post-restart challenge wave'. The operator sees a gateway forging or a failing challenge (I3) when the real cause is notify-queue latency. The ADR also does not say when the expiry clock runs for a challenge that was never sent. 'The expiry starts at the send' leaves the CONNECTED-wait unbounded unless it has its own deadline, and the 'within the expiry' clause gives it the challenge expiry by implication.
summary: D14 treats a CONNECTED that has not arrived as dropped and counts the session expired, which clears its record and forces a full Register. But at origin/dev the gateway holds CONNECTED and delivers it late under storm, breaker or directory-degraded conditions. Honest agents would be counted expired en masse in the reattach storm, contradicting S1's expired=0 and firing YuzuStateSignatureRefused

trigger: An implementer builds ADR-0074 wave 2's D5 per-session challenge from ADR-0074 alone
classification_rationale: ADR-0073 D14 now fixes the carrier for 'the same challenge D5 issues at the start of every session': a system-reserved __session__.challenge, the session_challenge SystemReservedPush, a mgmt-plane SendCommand for gateway agents after CONNECTED, the answer returned on the SendCommandResponse stream, and the bounded forwarder. ADR-0074 at 6942b74a7 (l.92, l.96) states only that the agent signs a server-issued challenge at the start of every session. It defines no carrier and no gateway transport, and has no cross-reference to D14. If ADR-0074 wave 2 designs D5's session-start challenge on a different carrier, for example a Subscribe or Register field, the reattach challenge and the session-start challenge diverge. That leaves two verifiers and two answer paths, and D16's 'challenge epoch' would be defined by two mechanisms.

trigger: an agent host powers off, sleeps or loses its network inside the 30 s challenge window after a reattach; or a gateway CONNECTED re-announce is dropped; in any fleet with routine endpoint churn

A ticket that fires continuously is not actionable.

The ADR deliberately excludes both outcomes from the alert and names only YuzuPgPoolSaturated, which does not cover a revocation read that degrades for a reason other than pool saturation, or a management-plane failure. The existing send_failed alert and runbook row cover resync, not challenge.
summary: A persistent `degraded` or `send_failed` reattach loop converts to a rate-bounded endless reattach cycle and a fleet that never converges, with no alert. The only cross-reference is a store-saturation alert that may not fire.

classification_rationale: The ADR says unsigned 'can therefore only come from a direct-connected agent'. Content is still refused, so the integrity control holds. What is missing is the rule that keeps gateway stripping on the audited, alerted bad_signature path. That is a missing required rule (I6), not raised to HIGH because enforcement itself is intact; detection degrades (I8). The via=gateway label on the outcome counter partly exposes it.

A gateway that strips an upgraded agent's envelope before the first verification on a replica (fresh Register, post-restart reattach, a CONNECTED-wait or send_failed loop it can induce) gets unsigned (no audit, no alert, counted as a straggler) instead of bad_signature. trigger: Slice 11 is deployed and the issuer's sweep stops resolving challenge_pending sessions (the sweep pass is wedged or starved), so the pending gauge stays high. That is exactly the condition the new second disjunct of YuzuReattachChallengeDegraded claims to catch.
classification_rationale: The ADR bounds the gauge `yuzu_server_reattach_challenge_pending` at 'at most min(--reattach-rate x (--reattach-connected-wait + expiry), the sessions held)' (D14 counters, l.~2069, and the S1/S2 assertion, l.~2889). The alert's sweep-stuck condition fires when `min_over_time(yuzu_server_reattach_challenge_pending[30m])` is ABOVE `--reattach-rate x (--reattach-connected-wait + expiry)` (l.1676-1677). A gauge cannot exceed its own stated upper bound, so this disjunct can never fire. At the defaults the threshold is 2,000/s x 330 s, about 660,000, which is above any realistic held-session count anyway. A server CLI flag is also not something PromQL can read unless the server exports it as a series. The edit removed the old working 'pending above 0 for 10 min without falling' condition from YuzuStateSignatureRefused, so a wedged sweep, which is a state-machine wedge, now has no working detector. That is an alert rule that parses but cannot fire (#2553). The share disjunct still works, so this stays SHOULD.
summary: The YuzuReattachChallengeDegraded sweep-not-resolving condition compares the pending gauge with the gauge's own documented upper bound, using CLI flags PromQL cannot see. It can never fire, and it replaced the working stuck-pending condition.

trigger: The revocation/CA read stays degraded, or a gateway's management plane keeps failing forwards. Each reattach of a gateway agent then resolves `degraded` or `send_failed`, the session is uninstalled with the record kept, and the agent reattaches again.
classification_rationale: The new back-off (l.2057-2060) counts 'consecutive degraded and send_failed outcomes per agent in memory (bounded by the sessions held, reset on verified)' and backs the agent off after three in a row. Every one of those outcomes uninstalls the session it is counting (l.2050-2056). If the counter's bound and lifetime follow 'the sessions held', the entry goes when the session goes. The agent's next reattach then starts from zero and never reaches three, so the loop the sentence says 'cannot loop unbounded' still loops at --reattach-rate, against the degraded revocation/Postgres path. The counter has to outlive the session and be held per agent, with some other bound. The text also says nothing about the next reattach landing on a different replica, where the in-memory count is zero. The S3 per-RPC balancing scenario makes that possible.
summary: The keep-record back-off counter is 'bounded by the sessions held', but each counted outcome uninstalls that session. Read literally, the counter never reaches three, so the degraded/send_failed reattach loop it claims to bound is not bounded.

caused_by: f6c581ddc (CS-R5F-R5-1 fix: issuer-owned CompletionQueue and stop drain)
trigger: stop() runs while the issuer's pass thread is starting a challenge forward, for example during a post-restart reattach wave with the challenge concurrency below its limit
classification_rationale: The new stop sequence is: TryCancel every table entry under the mutex, Shutdown() the CQ, drain Next() to false, join the polling thread. It does not order these steps against the issuer's pass thread, which is what creates new call objects and starts them on the CQ. Two interleavings are open. (a) A pass registers and starts a call after the TryCancel sweep has released the mutex. That call is never cancelled, so the Next() drain waits for its client deadline, the challenge expiry plus a few seconds (about 30+ s by default), which adds to the bounded shutdown budget. (b) A pass starts a call (ClientAsyncReader creation or StartCall on the CQ) after Shutdown(). gRPC forbids adding work to a shut-down CompletionQueue: it asserts or is undefined behaviour, and the process crashes during stop. This is the ambiguous thread-teardown ordering on my blocking contract. It is SHOULD because it is design guidance, not code.
summary: The challenge CQ stop sequence does not say the issuer's pass thread is stopped from starting new calls before TryCancel and Shutdown(). A call started after the sweep is never cancelled (the drain waits out the client deadline), and a call started after Shutdown() hits a gRPC assertion.

caused_by: f6c581ddc (CS-R5F-R5-1 fix: dedicated polling thread and arrival-time judgement, without assigning verification to a thread)
trigger: A challenge answer is dequeued while the verifier's revocation read (Postgres-backed CA store) is slow or degraded, or while it is being retried within the expiry as the degraded rule requires, during a reattach wave with other honest answers queued behind it
classification_rationale: The fix moved CQ polling off the issuer's pass thread so that a Postgres stall cannot age a queued answer into `expired`. It also says the deadline is 'judged on its arrival on the queue'. But the ADR never says which thread verifies the answer. Line 1989 only says the answer is 'handed to the verifier'. Verification includes the revocation check, which line 2051 says is 'retried within the expiry' when degraded. If that work runs on the CQ polling thread, which is the natural reading, one slow or retried revocation read blocks Next(), and every later honest answer stays in the queue undequeued. Arrival time is unobservable until Next() returns the tag, so the issuer's sweep cannot honour 'judged on arrival'. It sees past-deadline `pending` sessions and wins the single-winner transition as `expired`. That clears the registration record, forcing a full re-register, and moves the `expired` share in YuzuStateSignatureRefused. An honest agent's answer is then recorded as 'no answer within the expiry'. This is the same harm as CS-R5F-R5-1, moved from the pass thread to the polling thread. The promised test holds only the issuer pass in a slow lease, not the verifier.
summary: The ADR does not say which thread verifies a dequeued challenge answer. If the CQ polling thread performs the signature check and the retried revocation read, a slow read blocks Next(), and queued honest answers are resolved `expired` by the sweep despite the 'judged on arrival' rule.

caused_by: f6c581ddc (SRE3-R5F / PERF-R5F-1 fix: pending bound widened to include --reattach-connected-wait, threshold copied from the bound)
trigger: The issuer's expiry sweep stops resolving challenge_pending sessions (a wedged pass, or a sweep bug), so the pending gauge stays high.
classification_rationale: The second arm of YuzuReattachChallengeDegraded fires when min_over_time(yuzu_server_reattach_challenge_pending[30m]) is above --reattach-rate × (--reattach-connected-wait + expiry). At the defaults that is 2,000 × (300 + 30) = 660,000. The ADR bounds the same gauge at min(--reattach-rate × (--reattach-connected-wait + expiry), sessions held) (line 2069-2070 and the S1 assertion). So the gauge can never exceed the threshold: the arm cannot fire on any fleet, and above 660,000 sessions it is also at its own ceiling. The 'sweep that is not resolving' case the arm exists for goes unalerted. The other arm (degraded|send_failed share) does not catch it, because a sweep that does not resolve produces no outcomes, so the share has no denominator (the at-least-100-resolved floor keeps it quiet).
summary: The stuck-sweep arm of YuzuReattachChallengeDegraded uses the gauge's own upper bound as its threshold, so it can never fire. A wedged expiry sweep is undetected.

caused_by: f6c581ddc (keep-record back-off added for PERF-R5F-1 / ARCH-R5F)
trigger: During a sustained revocation-read degrade or a management-plane outage, agents reattach repeatedly and each attempt resolves degraded or send_failed.
classification_rationale: The new keep-record back-off counts consecutive degraded/send_failed outcomes per agent in memory, 'bounded by the sessions held, reset on verified'. But every degraded and send_failed outcome uninstalls the session (line 2054-2056: 'handled like degraded (uninstalled, the record kept)'). An implementer who follows the stated bound and evicts the counter with the session resets it on every failure. It then never reaches three, so the back-off that the ADR says keeps these outcomes from looping unbounded is never applied. The counter must outlive the session to work, so 'bounded by the sessions held' is false. The real bound is the set of agents that failed since their last verified answer, at most the enrolled fleet. That is cheap (100k small entries) but needs its own eviction rule.
summary: The per-agent consecutive-failure counter is described as bounded by the sessions held, but each counted outcome uninstalls the session. Read literally, the counter is discarded on every failure and the back-off never triggers, so the keep-record retry loop stays unbounded.

trigger: An implementer or reviewer relies on D14's statement of when the gateway loses a CONNECTED re-announce
classification_rationale: D14 (l.1946) says the held CONNECTED 'is lost only by eviction or a full store, which arms a registration replay'. At origin/dev, yuzu_gw_upstream.erl l.95-104 also drops a held notification without requeue, and without the replay that eviction arms, in two other cases: (1) when it is the probe and fails with a local encode exception (evicted with a warning); (2) when the server answers a request-class status (INVALID_ARGUMENT, NOT_FOUND, ALREADY_EXISTS, FAILED_PRECONDITION, OUT_OF_RANGE). In addition, 'latest wins' (l.215) cancels a held CONNECTED when a newer DISCONNECTED arrives for the same key. The ADR's behaviour is still safe in every case: the session hits the CONNECTED-wait deadline and resolves send_failed with its record kept. So this is a factual overstatement with no operational impact.
summary: 'lost only by eviction or a full store' omits the gateway's no-replay drops (local encode exception, request-class server refusal) and the latest-wins cancel by a newer DISCONNECTED

trigger: the reattach challenge sweep stops resolving (stuck pending sessions) while the ADR's own bound holds
classification_rationale: Line 2069 states the pending gauge is at most min(--reattach-rate x (--reattach-connected-wait + expiry), sessions held). Line 1676 alerts on min_over_time(yuzu_server_reattach_challenge_pending[30m]) strictly ABOVE --reattach-rate x (--reattach-connected-wait + expiry). A gauge bounded above by that quantity can never exceed it, so the stuck-sweep clause is unfireable by the ADR's own design. A rule that parses but cannot fire is invisible to every other gate (routed-concerns observability row, #2553), and a promtool test written to the spec would either not fire or would need a gauge value the server can never produce.
summary: The pending-gauge clause of YuzuReattachChallengeDegraded is `above` the gauge's own maximum, so it never fires.
